text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- PM Wim Kok says EU should reward Britain's positive and constructive attitude. (p1)
- Chemicals concerns Akzo Nobel and Bayer want to do separate tests of their respective vaccinations against swine fever. (p3)
- Supermarket groups De Boer and Unigro reach agreement on their proposed merger. (p3)
- Congress and trade fair organiser Amsterdam RAI reports 35 pct turnover growth to Dfl 305 million last year. (p3)
- Royal Dutch/Shell is one of 13 companies interested in acquiring a 30 pct stake in Poland's state-owned oil company Nafta Polska. (p3)
- Philips Electronics develops method to fully recycle fluorescent lights. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- FNV's union for the building sector is to probe its own dismissal procedure. (p2)
- Demand for workers in the building and construction industry is growing explosively. (p2)
- Labour Euro MP Piet Dankert says it will take at least 30 years for Turkey to become member of the E.U. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- U.S. container transhipment company Ceres and Amsterdam seek to invest Dfl 100 million in new terminal. (p8)
- Antillean island Aruba wants to become stepping stone for Dutch-South American trade. (p13)
TROUW
- Consultative body of employers' associations and workers' unions call for a better pension for singles and double income couples. (p3)
- Hotel concern Van der Valk claims 60 million guilders from Curacao government for lost income. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Liberal party VVD does not want Winnie Sorgdrager back as justice minister after next year's elections. (p5)
- Accountancy group CampsObers sees 1996 turnover rise five percent to Dfl 143 million. (p11)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
